leftEvidence.title: A child’s throne is named as David’s

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Light reaches the shadowed land, joy answers broken burdens, a child is given names of rule, and endless peace and justice are attached to David’s throne.
points.right: Eliakim receives robe, belt, authority, fatherly role, the key of David, opening and shutting power, and a secure peg that later gives way under attached weight.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places David’s throne becomes the location of an announced enduring rule inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places authority and security are narrated with both firmness and eventual collapse inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Isaiah 9:1–7 and Isaiah 22:20–25 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: The key of David is placed on Eliakim’s shoulder

payload.tension: Isaiah 9:1–7 foregrounds David’s throne becomes the location of an announced enduring rule; Isaiah 22:20–25 foregrounds authority and security are narrated with both firmness and eventual collapse. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
